reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) directly shows that separate nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces cohesion and causes ductility loss in CrMnFeCoNi, and E2 confirms the segregation occurs during high-temperature deformation without precipitates. However, the hypothesis extends this to a lower temperature range (300–500°C) and assumes slow cooling alone (without deformation) will produce the same nanosegregation, which is not directly supported by the cited passages; the evidence involves deformation-assisted segregation at 700°C.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces grain-boundary cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi
This nanosegregation occurs during deformation at intermediate temperatures (e.g., 700°C) and promotes intergranular cracking
The segregation is fast and occurs without forming secondary-phase precipitates
Rapid quenching can suppress diffusion-driven segregation, preserving grain-boundary cohesion
The ductility loss is specifically linked to grain-boundary decohesion from nanoclustering, not to bulk phase changes
